title: Volunteer Gwinnett highlights community service opportunities and celebrates parks volunteers
text:
Volunteer Gwinnett highlights community service opportunities and celebrates parks volunteers
Volunteer Gwinnett News, a monthly newsletter from Gwinnett County, announced on July 26 a range of upcoming volunteer opportunities and recognized the contributions of local volunteers. The newsletter aims to highlight the work volunteers are doing in the community and inform residents about ways to get involved.
The newsletter reports that volunteers are essential to Gwinnett County, supporting important projects, improving quality of life, building partnerships, saving tax dollars, and fostering community connections. As Gwinnett Parks and Recreation marks its 40th anniversary, the county is recognizing individuals who have contributed to the development and maintenance of local parks. According to the newsletter, "Since 1986, our parks have strengthened community well-being, protected natural spaces, and created spaces where people connect, play, and thrive, and volunteers have been a vital part of that story. From environmental stewardship projects to community gardens and special events, volunteers continue to make an incredible impact. Last year alone, volunteers contributed more than 16,743 hours supporting Gwinnett Parks and Recreation programs and 699,512 hours serving through Gwinnett's Youth Athletic Associations and youth athletic programs inside the parks."
The county is also preparing for the annual Great Days of Service, scheduled for October 16 to October 18. Organizations interested in hosting a service project can apply between July 13 and September 11. Approved projects will be posted for volunteer sign-up in September. More information is available at GwinnettCounty.com/GreatDays.
Several volunteer opportunities are highlighted, including fostering pets to help them prepare for adoption, volunteering at the Bill Atkinson Animal Welfare Center, and assisting at the sixth annual Back-to-School Bash on July 18 at the Gwinnett County Fairgrounds in Lawrenceville. The newsletter also invites volunteers to participate in the Buddy Hike at Shorty Howell Park on July 24, where volunteers will be paired with individuals with disabilities to support an inclusive outdoor experience. Additionally, multilingual volunteers are needed to help translate election materials and support civic engagement efforts.
Gwinnett Community Services continues to offer opportunities for individuals aged 16 and older to complete court-ordered community service hours. Details on eligibility, required documents, and scheduling are available by contacting the county directly.
Residents interested in volunteering or learning more about these opportunities are encouraged to visit VolunteerGwinnett.net or contact the relevant county departments for further information.
